To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of an organocatalytic reaction with a biocatalytic reaction in aqueous media enables the synthesis of chiral molecules in one pot, and that this approach has a great potential in the synthesis of biologically active compounds.

the combination of an organocatalytic asymmetric aldol reaction with a subsequent biocatalytically mediated asymmetric reduction enables the one-pot synthesis of 1,3-diols in high yield and enantioselectivity.
the combination of organocatalytic and biocatalytic reactions can be used for the synthesis of 1,3-diols.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, efficient and sustainable synthetic methods for the production of fine and bulk chemicals.
the development of new, sustainable and environmentally friendly synthetic methods for the preparation of biologically active molecules and the investigation of their mode of action.
the development of novel synthetic methodologies, which allow the efficient and sustainable preparation of biologically active molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the one-pot tandem reaction is a very powerful tool for the synthesis of enantiomerically enriched 1,3-ols.

the tandem process was successful for the synthesis of 1-phenyl-1,3-propanediols with high yields (up to 80 %) and enantioselectivities (up to 98 % ee), but only moderate diastereoselection (up to 3.6 : 1 d.r.).

the combination of asymmetric organocatalysis and biocatalysis in a tandem-type one-pot process is feasible and that the process window for the combination of these two different catalytic systems can be expanded to higher loadings of the aldehyde starting material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were able to develop a one-pot process combining an asymmetric organocata-lytic aldol reaction with subsequent biocatalytically driven hydrogenation in an aqueous medium, thus enabling the enantioselective synthesis of 500 mM loaded 1,3- diols.

the use of 500 mM aldehyde as a starting material is possible for both asymmetric organocatalysis and biocatalysis in aqueous media, but the combination of these two catalytic systems requires a suitable "process window", in which the organocatalytic reaction can be performed at 0 °C and the biocatalytic reaction is performed at 30 °C.
we developed a new tandem-type one-pot process for the synthesis of 1-3 diols, which is a very important class of chiral compounds in the pharmaceutical industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of organocatalytic and biocatalytic reactions in aqueous medium is feasible.
it is possible to combine an asymmetric organocat-alytic aldol reaction with a biocatalytic hydrogenation reaction in aqueous medium.
it is possible to perform a tandem-type, enantioselective, organo-biocatalytic synthesis in aqueous medium at high substrate concentrations.
